note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment options following confirmation of high-grade prostate cancer on recent biopsy and markedly elevated PSA.

The patient is a 73-year-old retired electrical engineer, married, living with his partner. He has a history of hypertension and COPD, managed with regular cardiology reviews. His prostate cancer journey began with a PSA of 4.4 ng/mL in April 2022, which rose to 19.4 ng/mL by March 2023, prompting a biopsy that revealed Gleason 4+4 adenocarcinoma. Despite a temporary PSA decline to 8.4 ng/mL in February 2024, the current PSA is 86.0 ng/mL, indicating disease progression. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 6/35. He has limited mobility, performing only chair-based exercises, and is alcohol-free. Recent appointments include a stable cardiology review in autumn 2024, thyroid screening with endocrinology, and a sleep clinic evaluation for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea.

Per rectum, a firm nodule is palpable in the left lateral aspect of the prostate, consistent with a cT2 clinical stage. The patient is generally well-nourished, with stable vital signs and no signs of acute distress.
